title: Slide Preparation for Mounting Samples for TissueCyte 1000 Sectioning and Imaging
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ber8jd9w
materials: 1x3 glass microscope slides with project-appropriate barcodes
Wooden applicator (Ted Pella Product 128-2 or equivalent)
Sufficiently well-ventilated area; Lab hood, or open workspace
PF0315: TissueCyte Specimen Embedding - Acrylamide co-embedding

Warning: Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor. Avoid breathing fumes from Epoxy. Exercise caution when using power equipment (Dremel). Consult your Supervisor or a Health & Safety Officer if you have questions or concerns.
Obtain all materials necessary and make sure the Dremel is fully charged.
Clean work area and put away unused materials.
Dispose of waste in standard non-biohazardous waste stream.

steps.title: Prepare Workspace
steps.instruction: Prepare a clean, safe environment for handling magnets and glass.

substeps.instruction: Find a well-ventilated bench area with sufficient workspace.
Clear all metals and electronic devices from the bench top where neodymium magnets will be present.
Wipe down the benchtop with 70% EtOH to remove dust and dirt.

steps.title: Roughen Glass Slide Surface
steps.instruction: Roughen the front side of the 1x3 glass slide using a Dremel rotary tool.

substeps.instruction: Place a 1x3 slide on a flat surface with the frosted side facing up.
Set the Dremel rotary tool to medium speed (~40,000 RPM) using a silicon carbide grinding stone or appropriate attachment.
Roughen the front side of the slide in the target area approximately 15 mm from the non-painted end (end with crosshairs).
Cover the whole area from top to bottom of the slide across a width of ~25 mm.
Push down on the glass lightly to avoid breaking it.
If needed, use a permanent marker on a blank slide as a reference for the target area.
Roughen the required number of slides one at a time.

steps.title: Clean Slides and Work Surface
steps.instruction: Remove debris from the slides and workspace.

substeps.instruction: Wipe the work surface and glass slides down with 70% ethanol.
Ensure no glass dust remains on the back side of the slides.

steps.title: Attach First Magnet
steps.instruction: Secure the first neodymium magnet (2.5mm x 2.5mm x 10mm) to the back of the slide using epoxy.

substeps.instruction: Separate individual magnets on a clean bench top, keeping them at least 4 cm apart.
Squeeze a small amount of 5-minute Epoxy onto aluminum foil and mix well with a wooden stick.
Apply a small amount of Epoxy (approximately the size of the magnet) to the backside of the 1x3 slide, 15 mm from the edge with crosshairs, avoiding large globs.
Using plastic forceps, place a single magnet in the center of the Epoxy.
Push down as hard as possible so the magnet is parallel with the glass surface and aligned perpendicular to the slide edge.
Place the slide aside to dry, ensuring it is far from other magnets to prevent movement.

steps.title: Attach Second Magnet
steps.instruction: Secure the second neodymium magnet to the back of the slide.

substeps.instruction: Allow the first magnet's Epoxy to harden for 15-20 minutes.
Apply a small amount of Epoxy 20 mm from the first magnet.
Using plastic forceps, place a second magnet in the Epoxy and push down as hard as possible so it is parallel with the glass surface and aligned perpendicular to the slide edge.

steps.title: Finalize and Quality Control
steps.instruction: Ensure the slide is level and free of excess adhesive.

substeps.instruction: Remove excess Epoxy on or around the magnets using a razor blade.
Use a small bubble level to check that the magnets mounted on each slide align to a level surface; discard the slide if it is not level.
